question.leadin: In 1962, this man was imprisoned for life at Robben Island.
question.text: Name this civil rights leader who became the first black president of South Africa.
question.clue: This man was attacked for his founding of the Spear of the Nation during the Rivonia Trial.

swap.text: Merchants from this empire and the later Songhai Empire partook in the trans-Saharan trade. This empire's ruler Mansa Musa disrupted the Egyptian economy by handing out gold during his trip to Mecca.
swap.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

question.leadin: This African empire had its capital at Gao.
question.text: Name this West African empire that dominated the region in the 15th and 16th centuries. Its rulers included Askia.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.leadin: Jomo Kenyatta was a leader of the militant group that headed this movement.
swap.text: Name this violent 1950s movement, a rebellion of the Kikuyu people against their European colonizers.
swap.clue: Evelyn Baring declared a state of emergency in response to this revolt and helped oversee Operation Anvil, which forcibly relocated people from Nairobi.

question.text: Since 1974, this country has formally demanded the British Museum return a collection of gold artifacts looted from Kumasi, the capital of the Ashanti Kingdom. This country was led after independence by Kwame Nkrumah.
question.answerHtml: Ghana [or the Republic of Ghana; prompt on the Gold Coast]
question.clue: The golden stool supposedly descended from the heavens into the lap of the first Ashanti king in this present-day country.

swap.leadin: Part of this leader's extensive list of titles included "Conqueror of the British Empire in Africa" and "Lord of All the Beasts of the Earth and Fishes of the Seas."
swap.text: Name this brutal dictator both preceded and succeeded by Milton Obote ["mill-ton oh-boh-tay"]. He was deposed after a failed invasion of neighboring Tanzania.
swap.clue: This man expelled 50,000 Asians with British passports from his country.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the African leaders of the 1980s.
question.text: Samuel Doe served as president of this country throughout the 1980s. His successor would later sever and eat his ear on tape before plunging this country ruled by an elite descended from American immigrants into a civil war.
question.clue: The film Pray the Devil Back to Hell depicts how white-clad women assembled in a fishmarket in this country's capital and threatened a sex strike, led by WIPNET activist Leymah Gbowee.

swap.leadin: Name some things about people with the nickname "Crocodile."
swap.text: Emerson Mnangagwa, the president of this country, is known as "Crocodile." Mnangagwa leads this country's ruling ZANU-PF ("zah-noo-pee-eff") party.
swap.clue: This country's first president was Canaan Banana, who was arrested in 1997 on charges of sodomy.

question.leadin: According to an oft-repeated story, Robert Baden-Powell based the scouting salute on a gesture made by this empire's ruler Prempeh.
question.text: Name this empire with its capital at Kumasi. The final war between Britain and this empire began with Frederick Mitchell Hodgson's demand to sit on the Golden Stool.
question.clue: That king was aided by Okomfo Anokye, who set up the obirempon as local magistrates and codified this empire's laws after it gained independence from the Denkyera.

swap.leadin: Because this regime required song lyrics to praise its government, Mulatu Astatke pioneered an instrumental jazz genre.
swap.text: Name this regime headed by Mengistu Haile Mariam. The 1985 Live Aid concert delivered relief to a famine exacerbated by the policies of this Ethiopian military regime.
swap.answerHtml: Derg [or Dergue; prompt on Provisional Military Administrative Council or PMAC]
swap.clue: After taking leadership of this regime, one man declared the Qey Shabbir against enemies like the EPRP.

question.text: General Mobutu Sese-Seko seized power of Congo-Leopoldville and renamed it this in 1971. This name is derived from the Portuguese name for the Congo River.
question.clue: That action and other Hutu-favoring policies led to this state's overthrow by Tutsi rebels led by Laurent Kabila.

swap.leadin: Name some things about the history of the country now called the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
swap.text: During Lumumba's term in office, this southeastern province of the country seceded under the leadership of Moise Tshombe. A Soviet-led invasion failed to bring this province under central control.
swap.clue: Moishe Tshombe ruled this region, which broke off from a country ruled by Patrice Lumumba.

question.leadin: This conflict was sparked by the death of Hamad bin Thuwaini and the HMS Glasgow was sunk during an operation in this war.
question.text: Name this war that lasted about 45 minutes and is sometimes considered to be the shortest war in history.
question.clue: The initial cause of the war was the death of Hamad bin Thuwaini, which led to a coup by Khalid bin Bargash, who seized the "House of Wonders" or Beit al-Ajaib - a palace located in modern-day Stone Town.

swap.text: Other Nigerian military leaders during the war included this general, who later took over Nigeria in a 1976 coup, although he transitioned the country back to democracy. He was so popular that he was also Nigeria's democratically elected president from 1999 to 2007.

question.leadin: The Medina of this city is often considered the world's largest car-free urbanized area.
question.text: Name this walled city home to the Qarawiyyin Mosque, which is recognized as the world's oldest university. It was the historical capital of the Marinid Dynasty.
question.clue: A rich woman named Fatima al-Fahri founded a center of learning in this city, whose most sacred site is a shrine dedicated to Idriss II.

swap.text: The emperor Fasilides established this city as the capital of the Solomonic dynasty. It remained the capital until the end of the Era of the Princes and the accession to the throne of Tewodros II.
swap.clue: Iyoas I was murdered in this city, which was built to control trade routes by the emperor Fasilides.

question.text: Gbeto elephant-hunting bands formed the basis of this group, which expanded to include units named for razors and blunderbusses under King Ghezo. King Agaja's regent Hangbe may have formed this group.
question.answerHtml: Dahomey Amazons [or Amazons of Dahomey; or Agojie, Mino, or Minon; prompt on ahosi; prompt on Amazons or Dahomey soldiers]
question.clue: The Dahomey famously used these female soldiers, who were recruited from among the king's wives. After the introduction of the slave trade, they often used Danish guns in battle.

swap.text: The Desert Column sent to relieve the Siege of Khartoum was intercepted by Mahdist forces at this battle near some wells. Tory parliamentary candidate and British national hero Frederick Burnaby was speared in the throat in this battle.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Abu Klea [accept Battle of Abu Tͅuleiħ ]

question.leadin: Answer the following about a Berber dynasty, FTPE.
question.text: They originated in Mauritania, but after a period of expansion in the 11th Century, they built the city of Marrakech and based themselves in Morocco.
question.clue: Guided by the preaching of Waggag ibn Zallu and Ibn Yasin, this dynasty expanded to take Kumbi Saleh, fought Portugal at Ourique, and defended al-Andalus from Alfonso the Brave at Sagrajas.

swap.leadin: Name these empires or dynasties that ruled Ethiopia, FTPE.
swap.text: Early in the 4th century A.D., it became a Christian empire under King Ezana. Ge'ez was the language of this empire, which conquered Meroe and was a trading powerhouse until it had faded away by 900 AD.
